frequency_question: How often do bills of this class pass the U.S. Senate within a comparable window given the observed advance signals?
membership_rule: Includes major federal election/voter registration reform bills (e.g., SAVE Act, Freedom to Vote Act, PROVE IT Act equivalents) considered in the Senate since 1995. Excludes routine appropriations riders and non-controversial bipartisan technical fixes.

cases.name: Help America Vote Act (HAVA) partisan precursors

coverage_note: 7 named major push cycles; historical baseline for partisan-led federal election bills passing the Senate without a broad bipartisan compromise is exceptionally low.
known_gaps: Excludes minor committee-only marker bills that never received leadership prioritization or floor scheduling signals.
skeleton: Legislative cycles for major partisan electoral integrity bills since 1995: 7 major push cycles identified, resulting in 1 passage (HAVA, which required broad bipartisan consensus and major scandal context).
multiplier: 1 hit out of 7 major partisan election reform legislative push cycles
validity_reason: Remains valid through the current congressional alignment and filibuster rules; would only reset if Senate rules or major party polarization structures change fundamentally.
